utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Loukas, I'm -- I was already informed about it but I'm glad to see that you managed to get the assistance of an interpreter so -- in order to, as far as I understand, to facilitate the communication with Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. And I could indicate that for the Defence today, Ms. Catriona Vine is here and Mr. Marko Avramovic is the interpreter who will assist with communication today. And I should also add that I wish to thank Ms. Petra Jacoby from the registry for being of great assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Ms. Loukas, are you ready to cross-examine the witness, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, of course, Your Honour, I made an application earlier in the week that was dismissed and in those circumstances, in light of Your Honour's order, I am ready to proceed in light of Your Honour's order. THE COURT: Yes. Thank you. Madam Usher, will you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you have given at the beginning of your testimony. You will now be cross-examined by Ms. Loukas, counsel for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Djokanovic. Now, Mr. Djokanovic, you, of course, gave two statements to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course you stand by those statements you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do stand by everything which I said whilst giving these statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And the statements are truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All my statements are truthful and accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And, obviously, before you signed those statements, you were asked if there was anything you needed to add; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, before signing these statements, they were read out to me in my language and then I signed them. I do not recall a comment to the effect of whether I had something to add.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But in any event, you were happy that in your statement, you'd given the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All my contacts with the investigators and the interpreters were very correct and at no moment did I doubt that anything could be, so to speak, planted on me, although I did, while hearing the statement being read out to me, hear some formulations which do not correspond to the syntax that I use, the sentence structure that I used. I have a very long and complex sentence which is not all that easy to translate. So that perhaps when I noticed that something was amiss in that sense, I would just define it by that difficulty of translation, but essentially nothing was different, nothing changed from what was my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So in essence you're saying that as far as you're concerned, the substance of what you said in your statements is correct and that there may be some minor differences of syntax; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, I just want to take you through some matters from your statements. First of all, you, of course, take the view that had Mr. Izetbegovic not changed his mind about the Cutileiro Plan in March 1992, the war in Bosnia would not have occurred; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had Mr. Izetbegovic adhered to his position, had he behaved as signed as agreed, it is my conviction that the war would not have occurred in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Serbian side was ready for an agreement and for a peaceful settlement.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djokanovic. I just want to confirm another matter. In February 1991, there was of course a meeting of the SDA in the region of Bihac and that's where the links were established between the Muslims and the Croats; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The links had been established before. At that time, they became manifested and practised, publicly manifested by the tying together of the two flags of the two sides, the Muslim side and the Croat-Bosnian side.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course it was around about at that time that you warned Mr. Izetbegovic and the Bosnian public that their action was a route towards war; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that date, Mr. Izetbegovic was not in any way whatsoever provoked to speak the way he spoke at the rally in Bihac in the Cazin Krajina. And as I had this opportunity to say what I thought about that event and I gave this interview to Mr. Zivkovic for the Oslobodjenje where I warned Mr. Izetbegovic that such a policy was indeed conducive to war. And in another interview in the Sarajevo evening paper, Vecernje Novosti, I stated that Bosnia had its constitution and what Mr. Izetbegovic was advocating at this rally in the Krajina could disrupt the theretofor and literally I said quite good and balanced interethnic relations between the Muslims, Croats and the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course that's what your -- your party was a multi-ethnic party; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The party was a multi-ethnic one.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, you also, during 1991, supported the idea of a National Council representing each nation in the parliament; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did advocate that. I said that the chamber of the Bosnia and Herzegovina parliament should be a chamber of peoples where key decisions would be adopted by consensus and that would be a guarantee for peace. That chance was missed out on and this chance to prevent the war was a chance that, first of all, the League of Communists of Bosnia and Herzegovina had, that had been the ruling party in Bosnia and Herzegovina before the elections. Later it was much more difficult to redress that mistake. When I say later, I'm talking about a period after the elections.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, in August 1991, of course you organised a meeting with the Muslim-Bosniak organisation with both Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Zulfikarpasic; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a panel discussion in Zvornik attended by Mr. Zulfikarpasic and Mr. Karadzic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And your thinking behind that, of course, was that Mr. Zulfikarpasic was much more moderate than Mr. Izetbegovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was both moderate and he was a much better analyst, he was tolerant, he was flexible and he was a visionary.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the events that occurred in parliament on the 14th and 15th of October, 1991, in that context, you were aware, of course, of a committee for national equality that existed; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, under the law there existed some sort of a body, not as part of the Bosnia and Herzegovina parliament, but under the constitution, there was a council for national equality.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And this question of the declaration of independence had attempted to be or referred to that council by the Bosnian Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the rally in Bihac in Cazinska Krajina, when Mr. Izetbegovic had announced the adoption of the declaration of the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Serbian side continuously kept warning what that could lead to and of course in this final stage, it also tried this as the last resort to refer this issue to the council for national equality for their consideration

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So when you said -- when this matter came to parliament, this question of the declaration of independence, and I'm talking around the time of the 14th and 15th of October, 1991, and you say that you said to Mr. Krajisnik "They," meaning the Muslims "... don't respect the two constitutions. Why would they respect the Assembly rules?" Your concern there was, I take it, that the Muslims and the Croats, as far as you were concerned, were acting in an unconstitutional manner; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I don't think your answer has been recorded as yet. I'll just wait for that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your answer, Mr. Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said was that's exactly the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Djokanovic. Now, just in relation to that, the -- I take it that your approach was that you didn't think that the Muslims and the Croats were respecting the legality of the political process; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right, and I spoke about this even before that October -- since April 1991, when at a multi-party consultations of the Serbian Democratic Party, I talked about this. This was a body constituted by the SDS in order to cooperate with other political parties in Bosnia and Herzegovina on certain issues that they concurred about. So at that meeting, which took place on the 20th of April, I said that one day in our Assembly we should harbour no illusions about that, that we would be outvoted by the Muslim and Croatian deputies.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, you of course took the view at that time that in view of the illegal constitutional approach that had been adopted by the Muslims and the Croats in parliament, that the best thing that the Bosnian Serbs could do was to organise a press conference of international journalists and invite the citizens for a demonstration; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, myself, harbour any illusions that what did take place in parliament would not take place, so I thought it was our only chance to call a conference of the foreign press and to tell them that we were afraid that this would happen in the Assembly and thereby also to inform the public and have the citizens demonstrate in front of the parliament building against such a decision which was threatening to all.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So your approach basically was an extra parliamentary approach, an approach outside of parliament, whereas it seems that Mr. Krajisnik still believed in the legal, political processes and that the Assembly rules would be respected; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, protest demonstrations are also our form of the legal expression of the peoples' will.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, yes, indeed. There's no disagreement about that but I was referring to the things outside parliament?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Mr. Krajisnik probably also, given the office that he held, thought that he could still do something from this position of President of the Assembly of parliament.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I guess you'd agree with me that he appeared to still believe that the Muslims and Croats would still respect the constitution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we object to that question. It's not very helpful to the Court for this witness to speculate on what Mr. Krajisnik believed. This witness was present with Mr. Krajisnik at that time. He would be able to inform the Court of what he observed at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, the question is whether he appeared to still believe, that means that it's not just -- the question is not about what Mr. Krajisnik believed but what he in his -- what, in his conduct, would appear that. But let me make a more general comment. Ms. Loukas, it seems that we're going very much the same way as the Prosecution did, and that is this case is not about whether a war could have been prevented, what political action would have been best to do so. This case is mainly about what happened in that war and I'm not saying that it's totally irrelevant what action was taken in order to prevent a war. I'm not saying that it's totally irrelevant to discuss whatever political moves that were taken. It certainly adds to a better insight in responsibilities for events, but, again, this is a case which focuses on what happens in the war and with what intent that happened. Although I made some observations in respect of the emphasis the Prosecution -- emphasis the Prosecution has put on certain elements of the knowledge of this witness, we did not stop the Prosecution, although there was quite some -- well, some critical observations about it. I hope, Ms. Loukas, that I do not have to make the same critical observations at the end of the cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can indicate firstly I'm only half an hour -- well less than 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must admit that you go quicker to this less relevant parts than the Prosecution did. I have to fully admit that, so to that extent, the performance is -- to the extent that the Chamber is in the position to assess the quality of the performance, but at least it better meet what the Chamber would primarily like to hear from witnesses. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I just make one further comment. Of course when dealing with a trial of a politician in the position of Mr. Krajisnik and his responsibility in terms of joint criminal enterprise and command responsibility, I would submit that a politician's respect for the legal political processes and the -- and his approach to these matters is relevant to the ultimate issue as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said, it is not entirely without relevance but of course it becomes more and more relevant not on discussions in one year before the war started. But of course the closer we come to the war, the more relevant it becomes and the more it focuses on the specific issues in the indictment, the more relevant it becomes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, in relation to the various conferences that occurred in late 1991 early 1992, just prior to the war, I take it you take the view that the recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the recognition of the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the International Community without the internal issues relating to the relationship between the Bosnian Serbs, Bosnian Muslims, and Bosnian Croats haven't been settled was actually a mistake on the part of the International Community?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the majority of the Serbs and the majority of the political parties never worked against the territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The majority Serbian policy in Bosnia and Herzegovina was preservation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, of the equality of peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina and its remaining as part of the Yugoslav Federation. So the international recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina if it had to ensue after the findings of the Badinter commission had to be done only after having harmonised internationality and interethnic relations on a totally equitable footing.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, just going to a document that was referred to in your evidence in chief, and that is the 11th Assembly session of the 18th of March, 1992. Your Honours, I've indicated to Ms. Philpott that I will be using this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We received a copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you. I also e-mailed the Prosecution so that they would be aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you just help me whether -- I do understand that this is step 1 of 9 from Treanor's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- 65 Exhibit. Ms. Loukas, was it on Monday or on Tuesday that -- it enables me to get the right transcript in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Was it on Monday or Tuesday that the Prosecution referred to the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was in the first session on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First session on Tuesday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, I think you have that document before you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the shorthand notes of the 11th session of the Assembly held on the 18th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, if you go to the first page of the Assembly session, you'll note there, of course, that Mr. Krajisnik, as President of the Assembly, is speaking and opening the session and that he proposes only two items for the agenda and that is one: Information on the last session of the conference on solutions for the crisis in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And two: Questions raised by deputies. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, what basically that session was discussing, therefore, you'd agree with me, Mr. Djokanovic, is of course the negotiations around the Cutileiro Plan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we object to that question so far as that is not the complete reference to agenda items for that Assembly. In fact, there are a number of submissions in relation to additional agenda items made by various of the attendees and we invite Ms. Loukas to reference those additional items as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, do you accept the invitation?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, Mr. Margetts always has the opportunity for re-examination and my time in cross-examination is limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, then our application is merely an objection to the question and we request that counsel withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, in general, quoting specific parts of a document which would -- or drawing the attention to a specific part of the document which finally would give not an impression of the document that is realistic doesn't assist the Chamber that much so -- but it's not entirely clear to me, Mr. Margetts, what you would like to have added because -- unfortunately, my screen is not functioning anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm happy -- Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm referring to page 3 which is the page that Ms. Loukas referred to. The proposal was that the two items that she referred to be on the agenda. The next question is: "Does anyone move to amend or supplement the agenda?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Margetts, if -- of course Ms. Loukas is now aware that if any amendment of the agenda would undermine her Defence position that that's what she'll face in your re-examination. So Ms. Loukas, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I would take it, Ms. Loukas, that being aware of risks, that you will be cautious.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, you'll also note that Mr. Veselinovic suggested another item be included on the agenda and that is that the stand of the Serbian Assembly concerning the latest developments in the MUP of Bosnia Ministry of Internal Affairs because the Assembly must consider the matter and make its position clear, and then Mr. Krajisnik says, that the Assembly will sit again on Friday or Saturday when a number of laws are expected to be adopted and that matters to which Mr. Veselinovic has referred should also be discussed at the next session, not this session; correct? Okay. And then Mr. Jovo Mijatovic suggested the Assembly consider how we should proceed with the application of the constitution and the constitutional act. And then Mr. Krajisnik points out that a number of related issues are to be examined at the next Assembly session; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's all correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I note that Mr. Djokanovic's answer after my first question was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That is at -- let's see --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think he confirmed what you said.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So then the proposed agenda and amendments were adopted as initially proposed by Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point, the specific item that I was referring to has been missed and that was the first one proposed by Dobrivoje Vidic which brought into some extent the first item on the agenda, and the amended agenda appears on page 4 and is not the agenda which was initially proposed on page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Let's keep going with that, Your Honour. I'm happy to keep proceeding with the agenda. I mean it's -- the document speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So initially, the agenda proposed was information on the last session of the conference on solutions for the crisis in Bosnia-Herzegovina and questions raised by the deputies, and then, after amendment, it's information on the later session of the conference on solutions for the crisis in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the political situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in Yugoslavia and two questions raised by the deputies. Are we agreed, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After all these interventions by the deputies, the agenda remained the same. It had these two items that we proceeded to discuss.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. The only difference was that there was that addition of the phrase "Political situation in Bosnia and in Yugoslavia," but in any event, as far as you're concerned, the way it was reformulated in the second instance was discussing the same thing that they were discussing in the first instance; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djokanovic. Now, going to this document, now that we've dealt with the agenda, if we look at what Mr. Karadzic has to say, he's basically talking about the negotiations in relation to the Cutileiro Plan and I think at one point during his speech, he's actually reciting the text of the Cutileiro Plan; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Karadzic speaks quite exhaustively about the Cutileiro Plan, paraphrasing some things and quoting others.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And I think at one point during the speech that he gives, he speaks about the institutions that will be formulated under the Cutileiro plan and I don't know if you can easily find the paragraph in the B/C/S, but in the English, it comes after -- there's this discussion of the issue of tax and taxation authority remaining to be dealt with, security at publicly events, hygiene, sport recreation, each constituent unit, referring to, you know, the Bosnian Muslim unit, the Bosnian Croat unit, and the Bosnian Serb unit of Bosnia-Herzegovina would establish its own institutions, constituent units may establish and maintain relationships and links. Then he talks about -- there's this portion of his speech, he talks about the institutions will proportionally reflect the composition and we do agree that they do so in constituent units. Have you got that portion of the speech, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you give us an indication as to the English page.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It's on page 9 of the English. "If we have 6 per cent Croats in our units, there should be 6 per cent Croats in the police, national guards, the judiciary, et cetera, just as there should be 12 per cent of Serbs outside our unit."

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Do you see that portion there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I heard nine, I read six, and I can't find it either on nine or six at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I have the stenograph of the 11th Assembly session 18th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: The English translation number on the top is SA 0257110, SA 025780 X, so I'm just wondering if we have different copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have exactly the same copy in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Page 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand at least our legal officer says that page 8, which, of course, is ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page -- gives better chances.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 6 to 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the part you just read, Ms. Loukas, appears on page 8 of the English text, the 6 per cent of the Croats in the police and the 12 per cent of the Serbs. Yes, please proceed. Have you found it, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On pages 6 to 10, you can find everything that Ms. Loukas has read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now, Mr. Djokanovic, in terms of what was being discussed there, it was clearly contemplated that within these constituent units, that, for example, within the Bosnian Serb constituent unit, there would be Muslims and Croats and in the Bosnian Muslim constituent unit, there would be Croats and Serbs, and within the Bosnian Croat unit, there would be Serbs and Muslims. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And when you move on further and on my version of this document, it appears at page 12 where Mr. Krajisnik speaks, in the -- do you have the beginning of Mr. Krajisnik's speech there, where it begins, "It is true that our situation is not good. The job is not done yet. It is true that we still need to go along way before we can achieve our goals." And he talks about his impressions of the Cutileiro negotiations; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have this on page 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, on my version it appears on page 12. I don't know if it also appears on your version at page 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The start of the words spoken by Mr. Krajisnik appear on 11 and it continues on page 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It's interesting that we seem to have a different version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we just compare, if you would not mind, you could also take mine so that I don't have any access to your personal notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, it seems to be that, Your Honours, mine is one page ahead of Your Honours' version for some reason which I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how it should be, Ms. Loukas. Defence should always be one page ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: We always aim for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would not mind to give my version back although one page behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I have a habit of collecting documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever you mention the number now, I'll deduct one.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Right. Now, we were just talking about what appears there in relation to what Mr. Krajisnik is saying and he's there talking about his impressions of the negotiations around the Cutileiro Plan; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And he's there talking about the fact that as part of the negotiations, there were maps that had to be looked at?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And that the Bosnian Muslims had in fact supplied a map as I think it says there, "We succeeded in making Muslims supply their own map." Do you see that portion there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, but I also recalled this particular comment at the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Djokanovic. And of course the HDZ representatives had their own map, basically all the negotiating parties had maps; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evidently.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, it is of course in this context if you go to what is on my page 13 of the document, which is where he says, "In this respect, it would be good if we could do one thing for strategic reasons, if we could start implementing what we have agreed upon, the ethnic division on the ground, that we start determining the territory and once the territory is determined, it remains to be established in additional negotiations whose authorities are to function and in what way." Do you see that portion that I'm speaking about, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is contained in the document I have here on page 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And Your Honours have that particular portion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We certainly have, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, of course, Mr. Djokanovic, what Mr. Krajisnik was speaking about there was, of course, being spoken about in the context of the negotiations in relation to the Cutileiro Plan; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the article that we talked about the day before yesterday when I said, "Who was it who agreed upon this?" It was the ruling parties that agreed upon this then that's fine, but if that's somebody else whose out of power, then it's a problem. Because if the ruling parties agreed that are the -- in power in Bosnia and Herzegovina then this is something that might be implemented on the ground because the parties had, as their voters, more than 90 per cent of the population in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Djokanovic, if you look at what's stated there, you'll note that the first sentence states that, "If we could start implementing what we have agreed upon, the ethnic division on the ground," it seems that if you adopt the view that he's talking about the Cutileiro Plan negotiations, then the second sentence where he talks about, "When we start determining the territory, and once the territory is determined, it remains to be established in additional negotiations whose authorities are to function and in what way." So Mr. Djokanovic, I take it you accept the possibility that what is being spoken about there in the first sentence is the negotiations arising from the Cutileiro Plan, and what's being spoken about in the second sentence is additional negotiations. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The witness has given evidence on this point and should Ms. Loukas wish to cross-examine him on that evidence, then we invite her to do so. But putting propositions to the witness that we haven't seen any evidence for is, in our view, not the appropriate way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this is cross-examination and I'm doing precisely what I'm supposed to do in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: The witness can either agree or disagree with what I'm putting to him but this is how cross-examination proceeds, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Djokanovic, you remember that you've given evidence on these matters that was relatively early on last Tuesday, the first session, and Ms. Loukas takes you through the documents again. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, do you need me to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No need for that. On Tuesday, when we discussed this matter, this portion of Mr. Krajisnik's speech, when taken out of the context of the entire speech there seems to indicate that the parties that were part of this agreement are still in -- dubious, we don't know who they are. But when you look at it, this is obviously part of the Cutileiro Plan agreed upon by the three ruling party under the auspices of an international presence, in this case, the European community.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Djokanovic. And also when you move further through the session, if you look at what is page 16 in the English version, that's where Mr. Karadzic speaks after -- well let's see. First of all, we have what I've just been asking you about in relation to Mr. Krajisnik, then, of course, you speak and you talk about the fact that Bosnia-Herzegovina should become a federation and then part of a confederation and the fact that the talks have inspired a degree of optimism for the Serbian people in Bosnia. Then Mr. Krajisnik speaks again about the ties and of course that's been part of the negotiation that the various units can have ties to whatever region they like. And then a man called Mr. -- you might pronounce that name for me because I'm sure my pronunciation will not be as good as yours.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know who this person is, Slavoljub Pologus.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And then you come to Mr. Karadzic speaking again and in his portion of the speech again talking about the negotiations, he speaks about "We shall have to establish a full structure of government on the ground because this is our duty to the people who live there: Serbs, Muslims or Croats, so that we can have peace." So that, again, is in the context of the discussions in the Cutileiro Plan; correct, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is all about the Cutileiro plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And then after Mr. Karadzic, Professor Biljana Plavsic speaks and she speaks about the recommendation that she has for the negotiators in future talks as to try and come up with a key to an arrangement which would keep the door open as wide as possible for us to connect with Serbian lands in Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And this, of course, was something that was clearly contemplated in terms of the negotiations, that it was within the negotiating sphere of the Cutileiro plan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And then you have Mr. Dragan Kalinic speaking about the Cutileiro plan?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it would be helpful for us following the course of this examination if our learned friend was able to provide the page references to these situations.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Mr. Dragan Kalinic is at page 20 of my version which will probably be at page 19 of Your Honours's version and I'm sure Mr. Djokanovic can assist us with the page in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is page 26.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So there's Mr. Kalinic speaking about the honour to be invited personally by Mr. Cutileiro. Then we move on to say, for example, page 29 in the English version, Mr. Jacic speaking about the Cutileiro Plan. Do you have that portion, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at some point, Jacic does speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And he says that, again, speaking in relation to the negotiations around the Cutileiro Plan, "That it seems clear that the entire territory will be divided into three constituent units." Have you got that page?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is page 40.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Page 40 in the B/C/S. Thank you, Mr. Djokanovic. And then thereafter, a number of different people speak, still on the same topic, and then Mr. Carevic complains that they haven't been provided with the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, apologies for standing up again, however, it would be helpful if the page references were provided.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's page 31, it's just a few pages on, Mr. Margetts. I'm just going through it in chronological fashion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 44.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And then Mr. Krajisnik, at page 32 in my version, which will probably will be 31 in Your Honours' version -- I'm not sure, in fact, which version the Prosecution are working from. Would you be on page 32 or 31, Mr. Margetts?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If you're referring to the speech of Mr. Krajisnik, that appears at the bottom of page 32 in our version.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: All right. So we have the same version.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And you'll note there, Mr. Djokanovic, that Mr. Krajisnik there refers to a conclusion and that is that the -- he refers to putting a proposal for a conclusion. He's just doing a summing up as a proposal for conclusions. Do you see that, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my version, it's page 45.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djokanovic. The conclusions, the proposal, the summation for the proposal of the conclusions is that the document drafted at the Conference on Bosnia on the 16th and 17th of March, 1992, can serve as a basis for reaching a final agreement on resolving the political crisis in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Correct? And that the rest of those conclusions there including -- "It is our estimate that the negotiators have not deviated from the basic concepts supported by the Serbian people," of course refers to the negotiations; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: The next part of the summation is that "The results of the conference do not fall short of the minimal requirements set for the negotiators at the conference on Bosnia by the Serbian Assembly." That again follows from the question of the negotiations; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I don't have an answer, Mr. Djokanovic, recorded there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krajisnik is asserting here that at that point, the results of the conference were such that they did not fall short of the minimum requirements set by the Serbian Assembly, so that they reflected the positions and the conclusions of the Serbian Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And as part of his summation, he says, "That all suggestions made at today's session of the Assembly will be compiled in shorthand notes and sent to the negotiators and then further that a proposal for the takeover of actual power and establishment of authority in the Republic of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina shall be prepared for the next session." That is of course again in the context of the discussions that have been occurring on the Cutileiro Plan; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears that the last two items have been compounded which, it would be our submission, that it would be appropriate that the witness not be confused on this matter and that in accordance with the course taken on the earlier items, each item be referred to individually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I feel certain that the witness was not confused by that because he does have the document in front of him and he's clearly a highly intelligent man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything indicated here is in conjunction with the conference on Bosnia and Herzegovina, i.e., with the Cutileiro plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Loukas, I would like you to not rely on the intelligence of the witnesses and put proper questions to them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take on board that I just thought in the circumstances it would be more expeditious in view of the fact that the document is in front of the witness, but if Your Honour would -- I can take longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You know I'm not seeking more time, I'm seeking precision. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So then the discussion goes on and then Mr. Zekic speaks and then Mr. Krajisnik speaks again, and Mr. Krajisnik speaks about the fact that "Nothing's agreed as yet. That this is the working material." And that -- well, you can see what's stated there and I don't want to go through it with you, but basically again, we're talking about the negotiations surrounding the Cutileiro Plan; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, could you -- I'm getting a bit confused. You started with the portion on your page 13, my page 12 that, "What we have agreed upon, the ethnic division on the ground," et cetera, and then we are quite many pages further now and suddenly, in your question, it appears nothing is agreed as yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to reconcile because you have asked the witness to give a certain interpretation about what was agreed or not agreed. He gave answers on that last Tuesday and it's not the speed but it's the superficial approach that bothers me at this moment, and therefore when you say "Nothing is agreed yet," I was trying to find it quickly. If you could give me the page so that I can see what we are talking about and how this is to be reconciled with what had been agreed upon as we find it in the ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's all on the same page. I've dealt with the summation of the proposal of the conclusions, then I've gone on to deal with the very next speech which is Mr. Goran Zekic and then the very next speech after that is Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that's your page number --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's my page 33. I've got immediately the three topics I've just dealt with are all on the same page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I find it. If you just give me time to read it. Yes, I found it. You may proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, just going to the portion we were just dealing with which is -- you see where you've got in your version of the document, we were just talking about the -- Mr. Krajisnik's summation of a proposal of the conclusions, then we went to the next page of Mr. Zekic, and now we're back to Mr. Krajisnik speaking. Now, when you look at what Mr. Krajisnik is saying there, and that is in terms of -- well first of all, he starts off with after Mr. Zekic has spoken, he says, "What can I say after hearing Zekic as if we had not discussed anything as if he had just now entered the room." Now of course one often finds that in political debates, does one not, that certain people act as though they haven't -- or perhaps they haven't really heard what's been going on but they're just going to proceed to say what they want to say, basically; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, speculation from this witness as to what undefined people tend to do in political debates is not helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the general psychology of politicians, Ms. Loukas, is perhaps not an issue that we would put questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'm happy to rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: In any event, we've got Mr. Krajisnik pointing out to Mr. Zekic. "Did we not say that nothing was agreed as yet, but that this was working material. Did we not say that one basic principle was established? But this principle was not included in the material in its final form, that Bosnia-Herzegovina was divided into three parts. What they are going to be called remains to be discussed next." So in terms of what Mr. Krajisnik is saying there to your understanding, you were there, is basically: Some things have been agreed, some things haven't been agreed. We're still negotiating. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well this detail, this comment by Mr. Zekic because we all laughed in the conference room. By the way, he was a judge of the lower court in Srebrenica, rather, in Bijeljina at the beginning of the war -- in Zenica, rather. So Mr. Krajisnik is talking about the state that had been reached in the Cutileiro Plan at that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And I think towards the -- let's see, it's in my English version at page 45, I assume that might be on page 44 for Your Honours. What I'd like you to find, Mr. Djokanovic, is a response by Mr. Karadzic where he says at one point, "Bosnia and Herzegovina," this of course -- we're still in March 1992, "was recognised by those who are supposed to recognise it, Bulgaria, Turkey, Iran, and Libya. Perfect. It could not have been better." And he says that, "The European community will not recognise it." Have you found that portion, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received no translation of your question. Yes, I have found it, it's page 63.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djokanovic. Now, going on there, Mr. Karadzic says, "The European community will not recognise it. I have warned Mr. Cutileiro both about 6 April and about Bajram and we are writing to Badinter that it must not be recognised and to the European community that it must not be recognised at all until these negotiations are finished." Do you see that portion there, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So basically the feeling was there that recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina prior to the international negotiations being completed in relation to the final form of the three constituent units would be a mistake on the part of the International Community?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been a disastrous mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I've finished with that particular document, Mr. Djokanovic, and we can go on to a fresh topic. Now, I want to move on to your arrival at Pale in early June. Now, just prior to going to that topic, I just want to deal with something with you quickly. There was, I think, in early June, a danger of certain Muslim soldiers, Green Berets, taking over an army barracks and when you arrived in Pale, you discussed that with the people at Pale. Can you just tell the Trial Chamber a little bit more about what that was about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall with precision in what state we had the inmates moving out of the Marsal Tito barracks, this is a military compound, of course, but this was a subject that Professor Koljevic and I myself discussed with the president of Serbia, Milosevic, when we paid a visit to him in the building of the Presidency of Serbia, prior to my arrival in Pale, which is to say, that morning in Belgrade. Then at the very exit from the office of Mr. Milosevic, he asked me to do my very best for the cadets to be relocated from the barracks and for us not to make a single false step. He told me literally nothing in that barracks, not a whole barracks are worth the life of a child. So when I arrived at Pale I informed Dr. Karadzic as well as Mr. Krajisnik with what I had talked with Milosevic about. I think some sort of an action of a operation had been prepared by a unit of the police of Republika Srpska to evacuate the cadets, I believe the Minister of the Interior Stanisic as well as Momcilo Mandic were involved for the operations and the Muslim side was aware of this and Green Beret units were on the ready the minute the Serbian special unit started this operation of evacuating the cadets, they were to attack both the cadets and the inmates in the barracks and kill them all. We received this information from one of the most responsible UNPROFOR people in Sarajevo that day. So that very afternoon I prepared a communique for the public, to say that we would not make inadvertent mistake or any mistake at all and disrupt our friendly relations with Serbia. So that evening, in the newsreel on television, they aired a communique signed by the then prime minister Mr. Bozovic which was formulated in very harsh terms, but after that, they broadcast our own release saying we would not make a single mistake and that we would do our very best with our relations with Serbia to remain friendly and for the cadets from the Marsal Tito barracks to be safely relocated from there back to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So what occurred there was there was a danger of the Muslim Green Berets taking over the army barracks and that the problem was about ensuring that the cadets were protected and not killed; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the principal problem but there was also something else associated with the Marsal Tito barracks in Sarajevo and the airport in Sarajevo. This was a matter of psychology of the people in the city whoever held these two facilities was actually in control of the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, getting on to what happened when you got to Pale, -- well, Your Honour, I note the time, I'm getting on to a fairly significant topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would start your new subject, perhaps we better first have the break. We'll then adjourn until 25 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam usher, could you escort the witness into the courtroom. The parties are not instructed to say one wrong word since the laptop of Madam Registrar is out of order. If one would look at the transcript as it appears now, it would ask for a redaction. So I instructed the parties not to say one wrong word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, before we went to the break, we were coming to your arrival in Pale in June 1992. Now, in relation to your arrival there, you basically were attending meetings every evening; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In our submission, that misstates the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any complaint about misstating the evidence, the other party is invited to literally quote.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour. I'm quoting directly from Mr. Djokanovic's statement. Page 13 of his -- the statement in English, "After I arrived I have, I attended meetings every evening."

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I understand it, the statement is not in evidence, however, the witness has given evidence on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It would be preferable to refer to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, in relation to that, Your Honour, of course I'm cross-examining and I am entitled to proceed in this fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the other hand, Mr. Margetts is right. This is not in evidence, so if you want to put that to the witness, it should be clear what you're putting to the witness, whether you're putting his statement to him or whether you are putting his testimony given on the subject. That should at least be clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, I'm happy to proceed on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I think in that instance, it would be useful for the witness to have the statement in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be given his statement and then we are talking about the statement, the first or the second one, Ms. Loukas?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: The first statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first one.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It's the first statement, Your Honour, the dates of interview from 12 to 14 February, 13th of July, 29 and 30th of September all in 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the last -- the page number would be, in English?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: In English, the page number I'm referring to is page 13. Your Honour, I have copies of the statement. Of course the Prosecution have the copies of the statement, but I have copies available for the Trial Chamber and the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said before, the Chamber has received the statements just for informative reasons prior to the hearing. So we have it in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I sent an e-mail about the need to have the statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, could you still help me out since all the page numbers disappeared while being copied. Are the last three ERN digits 829 or is it --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour, yes. I have a double-sided copy in B/C/S to give the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If I might have a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have your statement in front of you, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just ensuring that our interpreter, whilst I'm referring to the English statement, can immediately give the portion in the B/C/S statement that I'm referring to in an effort to ensure that this is expeditious.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, just going to your statement, and I'm referring to the portion of your statement which is page 13 in the English, and it's a paragraph that commences, "After I arrived, I attended meetings every evening with Plavsic, Koljevic, Karadzic, Krajisnik, and sometimes Djeric at the Kikinda facilities. Sometimes people from local municipalities such as Pale, Sokolac, and Serb Sarajevo also attended. It was not institutionalised, it was the beginning of certain work. The meetings were informal." Do you see that portion of your statement? I'm just seeking assistance from our interpreter to ensure that we have the correct paragraph, Your Honour. Yes, it's on page 12 of the B/C/S version. Do you have that, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do have it before me. I already had occasion to read my statement in Cyrillic in Belgrade last summer and it was already at the time that I noticed this imprecision, but I stated here in my testimony two days ago that we started working at 9.00 or 10.00 in the morning and that we worked most intensely in the afternoon hours. In the beginning, we would simply try to determine what our work tasks for the day were.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: When you were in conference with the Prosecution, did you alert them to this difference about the evening in your discussions with them prior to giving evidence today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my stay in The Hague in November, I drew their attention to this and to certain dates concerning some of the Assembly sessions in March, that they were not congruous with the actual dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I call on the Prosecution if there is a correction statement arising from that conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not aware of a correction statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Who did you speak to, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to Mr. Margetts about the statement and about some passages that were imprecise that I noticed because I had occasion to read my statement in the Cyrillic version.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And when did you speak to Mr. Margetts about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In November last year when I was attending this proofing session for my testimony here, but I have to note that I did not consider this to be especially important. I did say that we worked from morning until the evening and I stayed in this facility throughout the day so I was unable to arrive there in the evening because I hadn't been away during the day anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: In any event, this correction and other corrections, you say that you informed Mr. Margetts of during your proofing session in November of last year; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If Mr. Margetts would care to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, the issue is, I think, clear. Ms. Loukas asks ourselves why the -- she was not informed about any corrections the witness made to his own statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the appropriate course would be for myself and the others who spoke to Mr. Djokanovic to refer to any notes that were produced in those sessions and to provide some response to the Defence. I'm not in the position to provide a response at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we've heard that the witness said that he not specifically met in the evenings but was present there all day and that therefore the work went on during the day not specifically excluding the evening but certainly the emphasis is different. Would you please check your notes and see what the Defence during the -- well the next break would be the long break -- to see whether there's any other issue about dates which should be brought to the attention of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I am in a position to respond to the matter relating to the dates because I do recall that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It appears at the start of the document where there is a reference to an Assembly session. By the context of the statement, it is clear that the reference is a typographical error. I'm not aware of that matter being communicated to the Defence because, as I understand it, it was considered to be insignificant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And, in fact, self-explanatory on its face.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well yes, of course, I do not know what it is exactly in general terms. It is to be preferred not to leave the puzzles to the other party on what you notice, but on the other hand, if it's really an irrelevant issue or something which is so obvious that you do not continue to call each other by the telephone on a continuing basis. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas, and the issue has been -- is there.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: In any event, going to that paragraph, of course, Mr. Djokanovic, you would confirm that these meetings were not institutionalised and the meetings were informal; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked the whole day from some 9.00, 10.00 in the morning until late in the evening and I said that we worked most intensely in the afternoon hours because Mr. Karadzic seemed to be more active. In the morning, we would be agreeing on certain things if we had some of the ministers coming over from Jahorina then we would discuss matters with them and then in the afternoon, we would remain in the building, receive people arriving from the different municipalities who had not been really invited but who would come in and then we would discuss matters with them. I remember there wasn't a single day that we started out with greeting those present saying we're opening the meeting, the minutes are being held. I just remember that Mr. Koljevic, Mr. Krajisnik, and even sometimes Mr. Karadzic would write down certain things, would take notes of certain things, although we were saying at the time that it wouldn't be bad for the meetings of the Presidency to be formalised for notes to be taken and this was done in the second half of 1992 with the meetings of the Presidency and the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now just in relation to these meetings, Mr. Djokanovic, I just want you to confirm that they were not institutionalised, that they were informal; that's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not formal in the sense of a session of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, if you look at your next paragraph, it's true, isn't it, that during your discussions with the leadership, that you realised that communications with the municipal authorities in respect of civil matters was poor; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course you cannot offer any evidence in relation to what the communication was like in terms of police and military matters because you don't know what the communication was like in terms of those matters; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And it's, in fact, for that reason that you recommended that someone should go to the field; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course going on to the paragraph, the next after the one we were just dealing with, that's on page 14 of the English version --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, it's difficult to, in fact, see whether or not, from the question, whether or not my learned friend intended to elicit a confirmation of the paragraph that she was referring to in the statement, or alternatively, she was just referring generally to the reasons why Dr. Djokanovic considered they should go to the field, but her quotation of the paragraph in issue was incomplete and there is a sentence that's been omitted which precedes the sentence regarding the recommendation to go to the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm happy to quote that as well, Your Honour. I don't have a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: When one looks at the paragraph, Mr. Djokanovic, it also includes the statement, "It appeared to me that the leadership wanted to establish a state but it had not formulated the way it should go about establishing responsible government in the municipalities." And that's correct as well, isn't it, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And in fact that entire paragraph is true and accurate; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And when we go on to the very next paragraph, that, of course, is true and correct, is it not? If you want to reread the paragraph, but of course you have confirmed at the beginning of your evidence that your statements were true and correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, just from a practical point of view, Ms. Loukas, the statements are not in evidence. Are you going to tender them? Because if you say the next paragraph is correct or not, it's unclear what the evidence is.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I am going to tender them, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So that next paragraph is, of course -- I think that's where we're up to -- is true and correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of today's -- of my today's testimony, I stated that I stand by all the statements that I gave. Of course I take into account the different, perhaps, inconsistencies or imprecisions due to the translation process, so I don't have to confirm paragraph by paragraph, I do stand by the entire statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Djokanovic. Now, the other aspect of course that I -- that is also true is that these translation issues that you've referred to are, of course, not translation issues of any substance but only of syntax as you confirmed earlier today in your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So the situation is that when you arrived in Pale, you heard that the people in Pale did not have communication with the crisis staffs; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that question. My learned friend has just elicited the evidence that during the discussions with the leadership, the witness realised that communications with the municipal authorities in respect of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Margetts, --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- civil matters --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- may I point to you from what I understood is that Ms. Loukas was quoting from page 14, second line. "When I arrived in Pale, I heard ..." I'll just have a look. "I heard that they did not have communication with the Crisis Staffs." I do understand that there were other parts of the statement that would be quoted, but I think Ms. Loukas was correctly quoting this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And that if you go on to the next paragraph, the one that begins, "In cases when the Municipal Assembly is unable to hold a session." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Of course you'd formed the opinion that the Crisis Staffs were renegade from this legal establishment; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Knowing the situation in my municipality of Novo Sarajevo prior to my departure for Belgrade, I knew how the citizens felt about the work of the Crisis Staff in that municipality. Upon my arrival to Pale, the people there told me that they had trouble communicating with the structures on the ground and this is something that Mr. Karadzic also mentioned at the Assembly session in Banja Luka, and this is the only session that I did not attend because I was in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course you were informed by Karadzic that the Crisis Staffs acted as they wished and they had their own laws and brought decisions of their own free will independent of the higher level; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not Radovan Karadzic who told me so. This was my interpretation following my touring of the field that they were pretty much detached from the political leadership and then on my arrival to Zvornik when I saw that the local enactment that they had passed and that were published in the local official gazette, this was a confirmation to what I had heard from the Presidency, that the Crisis Staffs were very autonomous.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And I think, in fact, in your statement there in that paragraph, it indicates that, "I was informed by Karadzic that they acted as they wished, they had their own laws, and brought decisions of their own free will independent of the higher level."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it was, of course, your idea to work to organise the War Commissioners; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now -- and your aim was to establish legitimate vertical communication between the leaders and the municipalities; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. And of course your role was to establish the government at a municipal level and you had nothing to do with the police or the army and their activities and you have no knowledge of their activities or any communications that they had with Pale.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The activity of a republican commissioner and the established municipal commissions was to prepare the session of the Municipal Assembly by involving the deputies who were elected in the 1990 elections. Once the Assembly is constituted, it should establish the legal organs, that is, the executive committee and that's in accordance with our prewar laws and the president of the Municipal Assembly to be elected by the deputies within the local parliament and not by the citizens in the general suffrage.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So of course you confirm what's contained at page 15 of the -- of your English statement, the sentence that begins, "My role was to establish the government at a municipal level. I had nothing to do with the police or the army and their activities and I have no knowledge of their activities or the communications that they had with Pale." Correct? Do you see that paragraph in your statement there before you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Within my tasks, I had no contacts with either the police or the military until after the meeting in Zvornik, that was following the meeting attended by Karadzic and -- Mladic. That was when I was already a republican commissioner and we agreed that the problems related to the police in Zvornik, namely, the personnel difficulties, should be something that I should try to solve in my contacts with the chief of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, in relation to your visit to Vlasenica, you, of course, and I'm referring to page 16 of your English statement, which I think is in the B/C/S. I'll just check. That would be page 17 in your document, you indicate there that you and Karadzic sat down and spoke with Mr. Bajagic. Is that the correct pronunciation, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the summer of 1992, Zvolko Bajagic came to Pale and Dr. Karadzic and myself talked to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And Mr. Karadzic said to Bajagic, do your best to save as many people as possible referring, of course, to the Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that, in fact, does misstate the paragraph and I invite learned counsel to read from the paragraph that she is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas. If there's any confusion about what it says, then please correct it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I wouldn't have thought there is any confusion. The paragraph is in front of Mr. Djokanovic. It's there in black and white to be read, rather than my reading out the entire paragraph in light of the limited time I have for cross-examination, I invite Mr. Djokanovic to confirm the truth and accuracy of what's stated in the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then -- let me just see whether I have the -- it's the Vlasenica visit.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It's page 16 in the English version, Your Honour, in the middle of the page. And it's page 17 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but there are several. I mean -- there are several paragraphs in which --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It's the last paragraph in relation to Vlasenica and it's just before the heading Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So starting with "around this time". Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
