utterances.text: Your Honour, and for the record, I'd just like it to be clear for the witness that he is not responding to the question that was the put by Ms. Loukas. Now he's being asked a different question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Usually if Ms. Loukas doesn't get an answer to a question, she's able to ask the witness again, but let's just -- You want confirmation of this paragraph to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, then I'll have a follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please read that paragraph. Have you read it, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I have. This is not during my visit to Vlasenica, this is after my visit to Vlasenica, that is, Mr. Bajagic's visit to Pale and the Presidency. He came to Pale during the day and was received by Dr. Karadzic and myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It correctly reflects what you said in the interview? Yes, I see the witness nodding yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So Mr. Djokanovic, just in relation to that, you've confirmed that the discussion wasn't during your visit to Vlasenica but that Mr. Bajagic actually came to Pale and of course during this visit to Pale, Karadzic said to Bajagic, "do your best to save as many people as possible". And, of course, when Mr. Karadzic was referring "do your best to save as many people as possible", he was of course referring to Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Again the evidence is being misstated. Potentially there's some ambiguity in that misstatement this time. So let me be quite precise. It was not a reference to Muslims in general, it was a reference to Muslims in Vlasenica who had voted in favour of a united Yugoslavia, that is, a small group of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to that, the witness has the statement in front of him, he has just read it. I am cross-examining. The witness can agree or disagree with my proposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, whether the -- could you please take your earphones off for one second. Whether or not the line, "Do your best to save as many people as possible," refers to a category that has been mentioned before or whether it's a general statement, Ms. Loukas is entirely entitled to put that question to the witness and your intervention was not appropriate because you have directed the witness to an interpretation which is not the only one of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I have a right of reply on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In our submission, saving Muslims is very different to saving the category of Muslims that is described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, yes, of course it's different, but Karadzic said, and then the line that follows is, "Do your best to save as many people as possible." It is your implicit understanding that saving as many people as possible refers the category or part of the category that was mentioned before. Ms. Loukas, of course, with a leading question which is allowed in cross-examination, now tries to perhaps elicit a different understanding of that line from the witness and she's fully entitled to do so. And it's not for you to intervene at that moment and say this line should be understood to say as the Prosecution understands it. Of course I do understand. And finally, what's the correct understanding of this line spoken by Mr. Karadzic is finally up to the Chamber to make that assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise. I haven't made my point clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I accept that entirely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: But my point is this. Insofar as Ms. Loukas is referring to paragraphs in the statement, asking the witness to read them, and then asking questions which apparently it's ambiguous as to whether they are confirmatory of the statement and what was intended in the statement or in fact they are new topics and they are unrelated to the statement, I consider that that is a matter which could confuse the witness and as a consequence his evidence will be unclear. In other words, it will be unclear whether he is responding as to what he meant when he made the statement or alternatively, whether he is responding to the question what he thought Karadzic meant when Karadzic made that comment. It's that clarification, that clarity that we seek.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You could have done it in re-examination as well, but Ms. Loukas, at the same time, I give you some guidance. That if you say please read the whole of the paragraph, is the whole of the paragraph correct and then take out certain parts, and then put questions to the witness which would perhaps at a later stage need to be clarified anyhow, then it's a more direct way to get -- to find with sufficient clarity what the position of the witness, what the knowledge of the witness is. And if he's asked for interpretations of words spoken by others, to make that entirely clear whether his interpretation is asked or whether -- well, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I thought I had done that with the question but I'm happy to rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you please would. Let's keep this all in our minds and try to get the clearest answers. Could you please put your headphones up again.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, we're back on that paragraph again. The paragraph -- that last paragraph before Sekovici, which I think is on page 17 of your statement. We're still there. So in I any event, you've read that paragraph of your statement and you've confirmed that it's true and correct; yes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: In light of the fact that --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I would have a comment, if you allow me. May I give you this comment that I have on this particular paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, yes, it's up to you. It's better to hear the comment of the witness at this moment or put a question to him. Yes, please make the comment you would like to make.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said that we could accept this entire statement without the details, without invoking this or that paragraph, that means that I stand by the entire statement. As I have had occasion to read this statement, I did see some inconsistencies, some vague things from beginning to end which were not there during my interview with the investigators. So I actually associated all this with the translation problem from language to language. In this particular paragraph, there is an example of exactly that and that's why I'm commenting on this situation. Around about that time, Zvonko Bajagic from Vlasenica came to Pale and informed Radovan Karadzic and me about a particular Muslim from Vlasenica. That is true. Karadzic sat down and spoke with Bajagic. He informed us that he was unable to save the Muslims from Vlasenica who had voted in favour of a united Yugoslavia. What he said was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When someone is -- your speed of speech goes up so quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, the interpreter could not catch the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps restart, Witness, at "Karadzic and I sat down and spoke with Bajagic". Yes, and please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. "He informed us that he was unable to save", what is written here is, "he could not save the Muslims in Vlasenica who had voted in favour of a united Yugoslavia." It seems as if there had existed a plan to save the Muslims who had acted in favour of a united Yugoslavia. What he said was that he was unable to save -- he was unable to save even those who had -- who had voted in favour of Yugoslavia, not even those who had voted in favour of a united Yugoslavia was he able to save is what he said. And he mentioned family by the name of Sedlar. There is a surname in Vlasenica to my knowledge, but this Sedlar is also a craft, a trade, harnesses, saddle maker, so I'm still unclear as to whether this was a Sedlar surnamed person or someone whose trade was being a saddler. Karadzic said what he did say so that is the complete truth about this. That is why I'm asking you, Ms. Loukas, if we are going to go paragraph by paragraph, to read them precisely so that if anything unclear should arise, we can deal with that immediately as we go along because I have observed these kinds of discrepancies throughout the statement which do not affect substantially the truthfulness and substance of my statement, but some technical things, unclarities can appear and that's why I'm asking you to proceed in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And that's why we're proceeding paragraph by paragraph because you have said that there are these discrepancies of syntax, Mr. Djokanovic. So I think we're in agreement. Now, in any event, Mr. Karadzic's reply was, "Do your best to save as many people as possible." Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And as far as you were concerned, what Mr. Karadzic was saying was, "Do your best to save as many people as possible." He was referring to people, all people, including Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had Karadzic not said it like that, I would have left Pale that very moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djokanovic. Now, Mr. Djokanovic, I'm just going over to page 17 of your English statement. That is the first paragraph on page 17. I just need to confirm what that is in the B/C/S version. That's page 18 in your statement and it's the second paragraph on page 18. Now we're referring to what happened in Zvornik. Now, you indicate there that you didn't receive any specific information about war crimes that had been committed against Muslims in Zvornik from the Zvornik leadership and that you did not ask about specifics and you only knew from talks about "bad things that happened." Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course if you want to read the entire paragraph, the entire paragraph, and confirm it's true and correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Moving on to page 18 of the English, which is the second paragraph on that page and I'll just confirm what the page number is in B/C/S. Page 19, fourth paragraph, Mr. Djokanovic. If you'd like to confirm that that paragraph is true and correct.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course as you understood in your discussions that Mr. Mijatovic in the context of discussing the problems in Zvornik indicated to you that Arkan had slapped him.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And Mr. Grujic indicated that he was detained in a cellar by people from the paramilitary units; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, going on to page 19, that is under the heading "Reporting to Pale," and I'll just confirm what page that is in the B/C/S. That's page 20 in the fifth paragraph in the B/C/S version. If you'd like to confirm that that particular paragraph is true and correct, Mr. Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct but I'm not quite sure still whether Djeric was present because that was when I had returned that evening or that afternoon from Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just in relation to that, basically it's true to say that what you informed the -- what you say you informed the Presidency of was that war crimes were taking place and that people were informing you that "bad things had happened"; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that bad things, ugly things were happening in the field and that they looked like war crimes. I was quite clear in what I said. I said that action needed to be taken, that we needed to organise a meeting with those people as soon as possible to see what was actually happening in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, moving on to the next -- second next paragraph after that, you state there that -- I'm talking about the paragraph that commences "When I went back to Pale, I informed Karadzic and Krajisnik of all the observations that I made on my visit to the municipalities and all of the events that I learned of. I cannot recall precisely what events I knew of at the time and which precise events I may have reported." That's true and correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in response to a question by the investigator because I had talked -- he asked me whether I had talked on this topic with Karadzic and Krajisnik and I said that I indeed had talked with them and then he asked me a follow-up question whether we had talked about anything specific in relation to those things. And I had said no, we hadn't because I had no specific data. The municipal leadership people hadn't given me any specific information and then it was not my task at that time to investigate these matters. I just conveyed a general information to them about the situation in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So this general information about the situation in the field that you conveyed, of course, did not involve you actually witnessing any war crimes, of course, but conveying that "many bad things had happened." Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, I just want to move on to your second statement to the Prosecution, that is the one dated 16th, 17th and 18th of December, 2003. Your Honours, I can indicate that I have copies in English and B/C/S should anyone require them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have the statements in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'll just provide a copy in English and B/C/S to the registrar. Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I'm just letting the interpreter know that we'll have to do the same thing with the English and the B/C/S as we were doing with the previous statement so we can ensure that we're on the same page. I think everybody now has a copy, Your Honour. Does Your Honour want a copy of the B/C/S as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Madam Registrar already got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djokanovic, we're now on your statement to the OTP of 16, 17, and 18th, December, 2003. I think you should have a copy of B/C/S in front of you. Now, let's go to page 3 in the English, that's at the top of the page in the English and we'll just confirm what that is in the B/C/S. That is page 4 in the B/C/S. So it's the first paragraph in the B/C/S on page 4. So you have that before you, Mr. Djokanovic? Now, I want you to read through that paragraph, that's the paragraph that begins, "At the early stages of the war, the local authority was in the hands of the Crisis Staffs who were not elected by the people and it seemed to me that their wish to rule was very strong and that they wanted to take charge of everything and not yield their authority to any other state organ." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Apparently, it's actually page 3 in the second paragraph of the B/C/S, but you nevertheless seem to have found it, Mr. Djokanovic. Now, you've read that paragraph in its entirety, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And you can confirm that that statement contained within that paragraph, that entire paragraph, is true and accurate; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I also want to take you to page 4 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, I just heard you to ask the witness to confirm, of course he, in general terms, confirmed the correctness of his statement so what you are doing is more or less drawing our attention to the importance of that paragraph. You could even do that on the basis of the general confirmation of the witness if --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you would say that paragraph is very much in light of the general confirmation of the witness gave, I would very much like to draw your attention to that paragraph without even asking him to reconfirm that again. Unless there's any doubt in your mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour there's no doubt in my mind. It's just that the witness has indicated that there may be the occasional issue of syntax, or what have you, so there's no doubt in anyone's mind in the courtroom that we are dealing with the truthfulness and accuracy, the precise accuracy of the paragraph in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed. The only thing -- it doesn't make that much sense to us to ask -- could you please read, is this correct? You could do that with every paragraph and if there are no further questions then perhaps you could just accept the statement as being truthful.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: In any event, Mr. Djokanovic, as far as you were concerned your knowledge in relation to the Crisis Staffs was that they were operating on a pretty much autonomous basis and did not wish to yield their authority anywhere else; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way things looked; however, in those municipalities which I toured, they had accepted a decision to form commissions. There were no major problems, not the kind of problems that I would remember in terms of the transition to a new stage with the War Commissions actually preparing decisions of the Municipal Assemblies.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djokanovic. Now, moving on to page 4 in the English version, that's the second full paragraph. If you want to have a look at that paragraph -- it's exactly the same in B/C/S, apparently, on page 4. Just have a quick read of that paragraph and I want to ask you a question in relation to it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph is that, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It's the second full paragraph on page 4. It commences, "By only declaring a state of imminent threat of war, the Republika Srpska was able to organise itself as though war was going on but continued to act as though."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, when you say the second full paragraph, you mean to say -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Third.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: We have a half a paragraph on top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now it's clear to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And I'm referring to that paragraph that begins, and I'll say it a little bit more slowly this time for the interpreters, "By only declaring a state of imminent threat of war, the Republika Srpska was able to organise itself as though the war was going on but continue to act as though it was peacetime and therefore maintain the legal background of 1990." Do you see that portion of your statement there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And in relation to that, of course, whether there was a state of imminent threat of war or a declared state of war, of course, carried different legal implications, constitutionally; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The state of war was not introduced at the time. At the time, there was only the state of an imminent threat of war.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we're in agreement. The state of war had not been declared and legally, and constitutionally, what we were dealing with at that time was a declaration only of a state of imminent threat of war; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, moving on to page 6 of the English statement, and that is the second last paragraph which, in B/C/S, will be confirmed for me in a moment. So that, in your version, is the sixth page, last paragraph, Mr. Djokanovic. Now, again, in that paragraph, do you want the opportunity to read it so we can confirm that it's truthful and accurate and there are no problems with syntax?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now -- so as far as you were concerned, the impression that you had when you arrived in Pale was that the Crisis Staffs acted independently of the higher authority; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my impression, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And in fact, as an example of that, in Banja Luka and Zvornik, the regional and municipal Crisis Staffs did all the work necessary to create mini states; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just another matter in relation to -- and this is at page 11 of the English statement, this is the very last paragraph on page 11. That is page 12, Mr. Djokanovic, and third paragraph, Mr. Djokanovic. So I'm talking now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you are -- before we have any confusion, now you are not referring to the fourth full paragraph but to the third full paragraph on page 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, in the English, I'm referring to the last paragraph on page 11. In the B/C/S, I will just confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the fourth paragraph but the third full paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, it's the third full paragraph, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Do you have that before you, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have page 12 before me.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And we're looking at that paragraph entitled, "There is an interview with Alija Izetbegovic under the title Civil State or Civil War." Now you confirm the truthfulness and accuracy of the substance and the syntax in relation to that paragraph, Mr. Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified about this matter two days ago and we looked at these two documents here.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed. Now, Mr. Djokanovic, Mr. Zulfikarpasic, and we're talking Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. around end of 1991 at this point, Mr. Zulfikarpasic, the head of the MBO refers to Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, the leader of the SDA, distributing arms to his people through the arms of his party; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, that's what Mr. Zulfikarpasic stated in his interview and he talked to Mr. Karadzic and myself about this after the Zvornik forum when we stopped by on the road between Tisce and Sekovici in a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course you'd heard about this sort of thing not just from Mr. Zulfikarpasic; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to go to page 12, Mr. Djokanovic, of your statement, and that is at -- in the B/C/S, I'm -- now we're dealing with the fourth full paragraph on page 12 of the English, and that will be page 13, third paragraph in the B/C/S version. Now, you see that paragraph, "I don't believe there was a clearly stated plan set down by the republican leadership for ethnic cleansing." Now, just in relation to that entire paragraph, if you just want to check it for truthfulness, accuracy and no problems with syntax. I take it you confirm it's truthful and accurate in all respects?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything stated in the paragraph's correct except in that part where it's Karadzorde stated that if the Serbs wanted to defend themselves then every Serb must kill a Turk. This was something that dates from early 19th century, the first Serb uprising against the Osmans, or rather, the Turks, where he addressing the Serb warriors said so and he said that they should first start by rising against Subasas who were then -- the village to kill them. The village elderlies or the village leaders.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That is just a historical reference as you say to the early 19th century. You're nodding, perhaps for the transcript we should have a verbal answer. Just confirm yes rather than just nodding, that's all, Mr. Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. I will -- I would like to comment on this further by your leave, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour, I just want to continue with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness gives at a certain moment a point where he would like to comment -- unless you have specific questions on this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I do have a specific question on this paragraph and I'll happily invite the witness ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll give you an opportunity to give your comment but first, Ms. Loukas has a question for you in relation to this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And I assure you, Mr. Djokanovic, I also will give you an opportunity in my cross-examination to further answer, it's just that I wanted to ask you a further question in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now where you've stated there, "I don't believe there was a clearly stated plan set down by the republican leadership for ethnic cleansing," obviously, Mr. Djokanovic, if you thought there was some sort of plan of that nature, you would never have become involved as a republican commissioner; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. When I was looking -- when I was -- when I wanted to comment, I wanted to comment on the individual sentences written down here because these are my statements in response to the investigator's question. So when I said so that I don't believe there was a clearly stated plan set down by the republican leadership for ethnic cleansing, that's something that I'm saying in response to the question put to me by the investigator. And it is true that, at the time, I was not aware of the existence of any such plan for the ethnic cleansing of other peoples or otherwise I would not have been present at Pale at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You move to another paragraph, Ms. Loukas, because then ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'm just about to move to the next paragraph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I'd like then to have a clarification on the previous paragraph. You explained, Mr. Djokanovic, that there was no clearly-stated plan and you say, "It's true at the time I was not aware of the existence of any such plan." Has that changed. If you say "at the time", has that -- I mean looking back now, is it different for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, a minute ago, I said that I do believe so at present. I just gave one reservation because I'm not privy to this entire affair. I just can claim that I knew that they did not have a plan for ethnic cleansing. However, I also mentioned the fear that was present amongst the Serbian population and then I associated it with the World War II. But there was this moment when the supporters of the HDZ at their rallies were singing, "Hang the Serbs. There aren't as many Serbs as there are trees for them to be hung on." There was another poem that was sung by the Muslims from Trebinje to Bosanski Brod, there wouldn't be a single Serb or a single Croat. So Trebinje is of course bordering with Montenegro where as Bosanski Brod is in Croatia in Eastern Slavonia. In Croatia they're singing, "There aren't as many willows, the trees as -- as many Serbs as willows that there are. That was the song sung by the Croats, whereas the Muslims stated -- sang another song saying that there wouldn't be any Croats or Serbs left, just us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you said you didn't know about a plan at the time, at this moment you're still taking the position -- at the same time, -- in the same paragraph, you say so whilst there was no detailed plan for ethnic cleansing, the fear that the Serbs motivated them to react in the way that they did and resulted also in the crimes. That they did react in the way they did sounds rather vague and immediately follows on the line where you say that "There was no detailed plan for ethnic cleansing." The way they reacted, was that actually ethnic cleansing or was it not?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would first like to have the witness answer this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During my testimony two days ago, I mentioned the euphoria that existed on one side and that was the winner's euphoria on the side of the Muslims and the Croats after the adoption of the memorandum on the independence, or rather, the international recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Whereas the other side was enraged with the developments. Now I'm talking about the Serbs from Bosnia-Herzegovina because they were being deprived of Yugoslavia divided from Serbia and Montenegro. The Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina although a constituent nation there were being outvoted in the Assembly. Nobody took account of their plebescite in 1992, in November 1991. Everybody is recognising the referendum results, and as a result of that, Bosnia-Herzegovina is being recognised although we know that the referendum was only attended by Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you. I think you are now explaining why there was fear among the Serbs. My question, however, was in view of your statement where it reads "So whilst there was no detailed plan for ethnic cleansing, the fear that the Serbs felt motivated them to react in the way that they did." And I said to you, the reaction in the way as they did sounds rather vague and since in the same line you are saying that there was no detailed plan for ethnic cleansing, my question to you was, whether understandable or not, whether there were good reasons for fear. I'm not asking for that, it may well be. My question is whether the way they reacted, whether you considered that to be ethnic cleansing. I mean is this an implicit reference to ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The sentences that I stated here were an introduction to what I wanted to say and you just put a question to me in relation to that. There were terrible war crimes committed on the ground, ethnic cleansing took place, even genocide in some cases. As a human being and as a physician, that is something that happened in World War II, I'm sorry. Now as a physician, as a person as a human being, and as a politician, I'm trying to grasp what the cause of all this was. I don't know. But as far as I know, there was -- the republican political leadership of Republika Srpska did not have a plan, nor did Republika Srpska and The Republic of Serbia have a plan for ethnic cleansing of the population in Bosnia-Herzegovina in the Serb-controlled areas. What happened was on a massive scale. I said two days ago that my position is that all those who have committed crimes must be held to account and all those who did not report these crimes must also be held to account. I have tried to find any justification for this and that's when I thought of the Karadzorde statement when he was starting this first uprising, perhaps that might have motivated the people because one must not forget in 1990 at the rallies of the SDA, they talked along the lines of "We had been ruling here for 500 years and we will again, we will introduce Sheriat's laws." Once I asked in one of the interviews on the TV, I asked the SDA activists whether they were identifying themselves with the Turks from the Ottoman Empire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can understand your need for understanding what happened, of course but the first and most important thing for this Chamber is to first of all to establish what has happened at all. So therefore, so do I take it from your quite lengthy answer that although there was no plan for ethnic cleansing and although there was no detailed plan for committing war crimes, that it nevertheless happened at a large scale.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is inferable that heinous crimes did take place there in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I did not only talk about crimes but also about the scale. I think you said something about on a large scale but -- massive scale, you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct. That is also indubitable, it was on a massive scale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At this moment, I have no further questions. Ms. Loukas, I'm looking at the clock. It is already ten minutes to 2.00. I am already late. Could you give us an indication how much time you would need tomorrow for further cross.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think what I'm planning to do is to ensure that we have some time left for re-examination and questions from the Judges and I think the assessment that we made on Tuesday was that we would be looking at approximately two hours. In terms of the time left tomorrow, that would leave me two hours and 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And my plan is to come in on time and that's why I chose ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, I was informed yesterday when you suggested to start today at 10.30, I checked with the senior legal officer who said is Ms. Loukas aware that at least two hours must remain and then I got the answer that Ms. Loukas would certainly not need more than five hours which was already one hour in addition to -- that's of course if you now want to have two and three-quarters hours additional to what you have had today then you come far beyond five hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, but nevertheless when one looks at what Your Honour has put forward as the 60 per cent guideline, I'm already well under that, Your Honour, even if I were to go to six hours, I would be well under 60 per cent guideline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We left it to you at what time to start it today. Of course you would have had nine hours if you would have started yesterday, so therefore I got the information yesterday, so therefore I want to avoid at whatever point that we have to hurry with this witness in the very end and -- I'll give -- I'll make some further calculations and I'll let you know where the limits are.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just going on what we discussed on Tuesday in court which was that Ms. Loukas, please ensure that we leave two hours, that is one hour for the Prosecution and one hour for the Judges. So that's two hours. I take two hours of the four hours and 45 minutes tomorrow and I say that I will come in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time will you still need tomorrow? You said two hours and ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I would have thought two and a half hours, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But we have four hours a day. If you want to leave two hours, isn't it true that two and a half and two is four and a half and not four.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I see what Your Honour is saying, yes, yes, yes. Now I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have four effective hours a day, so if you need two and a half more hours tomorrow, and of course when I accepted your proposal to start at 10.30 this morning, I always take a tiny little bit of time for procedural issues that might arise as well, so therefore I thought if you certainly would not need more than five hours, then it would be a good start. But if you now say that you need, apart from the three hours, another two and a half which bring you far over five hours, I would have not agreed with starting at 10.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Perhaps we're at cross purposes, Your Honour. I entirely understand your point and the way I propose is that we will certainly leave the two hours as agreed on Tuesday for the Prosecution and for the Judges questions. There's no question of that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This would suggest then that you finish by approximately the first break or shortly after that, perhaps shortly after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll let you know through the senior legal officer how this Chamber considers two hours to be, that's 120 minutes. We will ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00 in the same courtroom, and I apologise -- my apologies for the interpreters and the technicians that have we have again stolen 10 minutes of your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 18th day of March, 2005, at 1.57 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.57 p.m.,
